riskFactors.title: Unprotected Sexual Contact
riskFactors.description: Unprotected sex remains the primary transmission route globally, accounting for over 70% of all new HIV infections.

riskFactors.title: People Who Inject Drugs
riskFactors.description: Sharing needles or syringes is responsible for approximately 8% of new HIV infections globally but much higher in Eastern Europe and Central Asia.

riskFactors.title: Stigma & Late Diagnosis
riskFactors.description: HIV-related stigma prevents testing and treatment access. 14% of people with HIV still don't know their status globally.

riskFactors.title: Mother-to-Child Transmission
riskFactors.description: Without treatment, an HIV-positive mother has a 15–45% chance of transmitting HIV during pregnancy, birth, or breastfeeding. ART reduces this to under 5%.

riskFactors.title: Treatment Access Gaps
riskFactors.description: Only 77% of people living with HIV globally are on antiretroviral therapy. Gaps remain largest in West and Central Africa.

didYouKnow: U=U (Undetectable = Untransmittable): People on effective ART with an undetectable viral load cannot sexually transmit HIV.
The UNAIDS 95-95-95 targets aim for 95% of PLHIV diagnosed, 95% of diagnosed on treatment, and 95% of those virally suppressed by 2025.
PrEP (pre-exposure prophylaxis) reduces HIV risk by over 99% when taken consistently.
Sub-Saharan Africa accounts for 63% of all people living with HIV despite representing only 14% of the global population.

faq.q: Is HIV still a death sentence in 2026?
faq.a: No. With modern antiretroviral therapy (ART), people living with HIV can have a near-normal life expectancy. ART suppresses the virus to undetectable levels, protecting both health and preventing transmission.

U=U stands for Undetectable = Untransmittable. People living with HIV who are on effective ART and maintain an undetectable viral load cannot sexually transmit HIV to their partners. This is now supported by extensive clinical evidence.

By 2025, UNAIDS aims for 95% of all people living with HIV to know their status, 95% of those diagnosed to be on ART, and 95% of those on ART to achieve viral suppression. Meeting this target would effectively end AIDS as a public health threat.
